what: RFC 3161 time-stamp tokens over the SHA-256 of three signed cic-primitives release records, obtained from the DigiCert public time-stamp authority on 2026-11-03, before the certificate chain of those records ends on 2026-12-31. A token shows that the digest existed no later than the time it states; it shows nothing about who signed the record or whether the release is genuine.

authority.name: DigiCert public RFC 3161 time-stamp authority
authority.transport_note: plain HTTP (port 443 did not answer from the machine that made the requests); the reply is signed, its integrity does not rest on the transport
authority.terms_note: No terms of use for the public endpoint were found: neither the search nor DigiCert's documentation pages state who may use it or restrict its use; they describe it for code signing. Only a SHA-256 digest, an algorithm identifier, a random nonce and a request for the TSA certificate were sent.

trust_anchor.note: The reply carries a cross-signed DigiCert Trusted Root G4 (issuer DigiCert Assured ID Root CA, valid to 2031-11-09) with the same public key. It is NOT used as the anchor; the self-signed root (valid to 2038-01-15) is.
